name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China extended its pause on rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; Trump–Xi talks due at APEC
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of some rare-earth, battery and graphite export controls to 10 Jan 2027, a day before it was due to lapse; controls on seven rare earths from April 2025 stay in force (S&P Global). The extension is part of a wider suspension of Chinese countermeasures and tariffs while Beijing negotiates a lasting deal, with Trump due to meet Xi at APEC in Shenzhen later in November (The Star, citing Reuters). Watch is kept as the truce is short-term.
for_you: Short truces leave costs uncertain for firms that import from or export to China, especially goods using rare earths such as electronics and vehicles. Prices and supply can shift when deadlines approach.
rubric_hit: Major tariffs threatened between large economies; US–China measures suspended only to 10 Jan 2027 (Watch)

sources.title: S&P Global — China extends rare earth export suspension to January 2027

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
